#1. Find the prime factorization of:
(a) 487.
(b) 6600.
Solution
Solution:
(a) If we try to divide 487 by all primes from 2 to 1√487] = 22 (that is, 2, 3, 5, 7. 11. 13, 17, 19), we find that none
of these divides 487 without a remainder. Therefore 487 is prime.
(b) Begin by writing 6600 as any product of smaller positive factors, such as 660066 100. We continue this
process until only primes are obtained:
6600 = 66-100
-(6-11X10-10)
=(2-3-11)-(2-5-2-5)
=2³-3-52-11.
If we initially factor 6600 in a different way, such as 6-1100, we would still arrive at the same product of prime
factors.
Prof. Eunwoo Kim (Chung Ang University)
